introductoryTafseer: Surah Al-Mulk, known in authentic hadith as 'Al-Mani'ah' (The Defender) and 'Al-Munjiyah' (The Deliverer), is a thirty-verse chapter that intercedes for its reader until forgiveness is secured and shields them from the punishment of the grave. In Ma'ariful Qur'an, Mufti Muhammad Shafi provides a luminous exposition on the purpose of life and death, the flawless architecture of the cosmos, and total reliance upon the All-Merciful.

historicalContext.background: Revealed in Makkah, Surah Al-Mulk addressed the stubborn materialists of Quraysh who concealed their whispers in hostility against the Prophet, assuring them that Allah possesses all-encompassing knowledge of what is whispered in the breasts, holding supreme dominion over the celestial spheres and the sustenance drawn from the earth.

sections.title: The Purpose of Life and Death & The Flawless Cosmic Architecture
sections.arabicText: تَبَارَكَ الَّذِي بِيَدِهِ الْمُلْكُ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ ۝ الَّذِي خَلَقَ الْمَوْتَ وَالْحَيَاةَ لِيَبْلُوَكُمْ أَيُّكُمْ أَحْسَنُ عَمَلًا ۚ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْغَفُورُ ۝ الَّذِي خَلَقَ سَبْعَ سَمَاوَاتٍ طِبَاقًا ۖ مَّا تَرَىٰ فِي خَلْقِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ مِن تَفَاوُتٍ ۖ فَارْجِعِ الْبَصَرَ هَلْ تَرَىٰ مِن فُطُورٍ ۝ ثُمَّ ارْجِعِ الْبَصَرَ كَرَّتَيْنِ يَنقَلِبْ إِلَيْكَ الْبَصَرُ خَاسِئًا وَهُوَ حَسِيرٌ ۝
sections.translation: Blessed is He in whose hand is the [Mulk] (Dominion), and He is over all things competent ۝ He who created death and life to test you as to which of you is best in deed—and He is the Exalted in Might, the Forgiving ۝ He who created seven heavens in layers. You see no flaw in the creation of the [Rahman] (All-Merciful). So turn your gaze again: do you see any rift? ۝ Then return your gaze twice again; your vision will return to you humbled and exhausted. ۝

phraseCards.englishPhrase: Exalted and blessed is He in whose hand is all sovereignty
Who created death and life to test you

vocabulary.meaning: In order to examine and test you

sections.commentary:
In Ma'ariful Qur'an, Mufti Muhammad Shafi highlights the profound priority in verse 2: Allah mentions the creation of 'Death' before 'Life'. Death is not mere non-existence; it is a created portal of transition from this fleeting trial to eternal recompense. The verse does not say 'which of you produces the most deeds' (aktharu 'amala), but 'which of you is BEST in deed' (ahsanu 'amala). Classical commentators like Fudayl ibn 'Iyad explain that 'best in deed' means deeds done with pure sincere intention (Ikhlas) and in strict conformity with the Prophetic Sunnah (Ittiba').

The surah then challenges human skepticism through cosmic contemplation: look into the depths of the skies and search for any flaw, structural crack, or irregularity in the vast vault of the heavens. No matter how many times telescopes or eyes scrutinize the cosmos, human sight returns humbled, fatigued, and overwhelmed by the majesty of the Creator.

subsections.title: Sunnah Rulings on Daily Recitation of Surah Al-Mulk
subsections.content: Mufti Muhammad Shafi cites the authentic hadith in Sunan al-Tirmidhi: 'There is a surah of thirty verses in the Quran which will intercede for a person until he is forgiven: Tabarak alladhi bi-yadihi al-Mulk.' It is an established Sunnah to recite Surah Al-Mulk every night before sleep to attain immunity from the trials of the grave.

subsections.title: Quality of Deeds (Ahsanu 'Amala) Over Quantity
subsections.content: Ma'ariful Qur'an emphasizes that in the divine scale of the hereafter, weight matters far more than volume. A single sincere prayer with a present heart outweighs a mountain of ritualistic motions devoid of mindfulness.

curatedTerms.literalMeaning: Sovereign possession, royal dominion, and governance.
curatedTerms.theologicalContext: Allah's supreme and undivided authority over every atom of the seen and unseen universe.
